# Session ID Resolution — Reference

> Part of the [ab-chat-session-management](SKILL.md) skill. For the 5-phase session lifecycle with per-store categorization, see [session-lifecycle.md](session-lifecycle.md). For frontend hydration and session browser UIs, see [frontend-hydration.md](frontend-hydration.md).

## Session ID Resolution

The effective session ID follows a fallback chain, resolved differently at the component and API levels.

### Component side (`AgentChatSurface.razor`)

```
EffectiveSessionId =
    SessionId (parameter)     ← explicit override
    ?? CircuitSessionId       ← ComponentRegistry.SessionId (per-circuit GUID)

EffectiveConversationSessionId =
    AgentConversationScope.BuildSessionKey(
        EffectiveSessionId,
        _selectedAgent,
        IsolateConversationsByAgent)
    └─ When isolation is ON:  "{sessionId}::agent::{agentName}"
    └─ When isolation is OFF: "{sessionId}" (same as EffectiveSessionId)
```

### API side (`AgentTurnRequest.cs`)

```
GetEffectiveSessionId() =
    SessionId (field)         ← explicit
    ?? Context["session_id"]  ← from request context dictionary
    ?? "global"               ← ultimate fallback
```

## SessionId: Type, Initialization, and Storage

### Data Type

`SessionId` is a **`string`** at every layer:

| Layer | Type | Nullable? |
|---|---|---|
| Blazor component parameter | `string?` | `null` → falls back to circuit GUID |
| `AgentChatWidget` parameter | `string?` | `null` → falls back internally |
| `AgentRemoteChatSurface` parameter | `string` | Default: `"remote-chat-{Guid.NewGuid():N}"` |
| `AgentTurnRequest` field | `string?` | `null` → falls back to context dictionary |
| `AgentTurnRequest.GetEffectiveSessionId()` return | `string` | Never `null` — returns `"global"` as last resort |
| `IConversationStore` methods | `string` | Never `null` — `ArgumentException` thrown if empty/whitespace |
| `ConversationHistory.SessionId` | `string` | Required record property |
| `ConcurrentDictionary` key (both stores) | `string` | `OrdinalIgnoreCase` comparer |
| JSON file key | `string` | Serialized as JSON object key |

The comparer across all stores is **`StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase`** — `"session-A"` and `"SESSION-A"` are treated as the same session.

### Who Initializes the SessionId — And Where

There are **four distinct initialization patterns**, each with a different owner.

#### Pattern 1 — Auto-generated by the backend (default, no-parameter)

When no `SessionId` is provided, the backend circuit generates one automatically from a GUID. **The GUID is opaque** — 32 hex characters with no semantic meaning. It cannot be recomputed from user data or route information.

##### How the GUID is created

Two separate `Scoped` DI services each produce their own GUID at construction time. They are registered in `AgentBlazorServiceCollectionExtensions.cs`:

```csharp
// Scoped = one instance per Blazor circuit (i.e., per browser tab/connection)
services.TryAddScoped<IAgentComponentRegistry, CircuitAgentComponentRegistry>();
services.TryAddScoped<IAgentChatSessionState, AgentChatSessionState>();
```

| Service | Class | GUID source |
|---|---|---|
| `IAgentComponentRegistry` → `CircuitAgentComponentRegistry` | wraps `InMemoryAgentComponentRegistry` | `string SessionId { get; } = Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N");` — **field initializer** on `InMemoryAgentComponentRegistry` |
| `IAgentChatSessionState` → `AgentChatSessionState` | standalone class | `public string SessionId { get; } = Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N");` — **field initializer** |

Both use `Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N")` producing a 32-character hex string: `"d1e9a3f2b8c04a5e9d7f6c1b2a3d4e5f"`. The `"N"` format specifier removes hyphens.

**Timing**: The GUID is generated once during object construction (field initializer runs before the constructor body). It is **immutable** for the lifetime of that instance — there is no setter, only a `{ get; }` init-only property.

##### What a "Blazor circuit" is

In Blazor Server (InteractiveServer render mode), a **circuit** is the server-side representation of a single client connection. It is created when the client first connects (SignalR handshake), and disposed when:
- The user closes the browser tab or navigates away
- The connection times out (default: ~30 seconds of disconnect)
- The server recycles the circuit due to resource pressure

Each circuit gets its own **Scoped** DI scope. Every `@inject` or `@rendermode InteractiveServer` component within that tab shares the same scoped service instances. Two browser tabs open to the same page get **two independent circuits** with **two different GUIDs**.

##### How CircuitAgentComponentRegistry wires the GUID

```
Construction order (DI creates this chain automatically):
  1. AgentComponentRegistryHub (singleton) — already exists
  2. CircuitAgentComponentRegistry (scoped) — constructor receives the hub
       ├─ creates new InMemoryAgentComponentRegistry (field initializer → GUID generated here)
       └─ calls _hub.Register(SessionId, this)    ← registers GUID → itself in singleton hub
  3. Any component @injecting IAgentComponentRegistry gets this scoped instance

On Dispose (circuit ends):
  CircuitAgentComponentRegistry.Dispose()
    └─ _hub.Remove(SessionId)  ← deregisters from singleton hub
    └─ The GUID and its registry are orphaned (GC collects them)
```

The `AgentComponentRegistryHub` is a **singleton** `ConcurrentDictionary<string, IAgentComponentRegistry>` that maps session IDs to their circuit's registry. The runtime uses it to find the correct circuit's components when processing an `AgentTurnRequest`:

```csharp
// AgentComponentRegistryHub.cs
public bool TryGet(string sessionId, out IAgentComponentRegistry registry)
    => _registries.TryGetValue(sessionId, out registry!);
```

##### How the chat surface reads the circuit GUID

`AgentChatSurface.razor` injects `IAgentComponentRegistry` (scoped) and reads its `SessionId`:

```razor
@inject IAgentComponentRegistry ComponentRegistry

@code {
    // Line ~525
    private string CircuitSessionId => ComponentRegistry.SessionId;

    // Line ~614 — used as the fallback when no explicit SessionId is given
    private string EffectiveSessionId =>
        string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(SessionId)
            ? CircuitSessionId
            : SessionId.Trim();
}
```

Since both the registry and the chat surface are in the same Scoped DI scope (same circuit), `ComponentRegistry.SessionId` is stable for the entire page lifetime.

##### Default behavior in practice

- **New browser tab** → new SignalR connection → new circuit → new `CircuitAgentComponentRegistry` → new GUID → new session in the store on first turn
- **Page refresh (F5)** → old circuit disconnects and its GUID is deregistered from the hub → new circuit created with a new GUID → UI references a *new* session ID → the old session still exists in `IConversationStore` but is no longer referenced by the UI. It remains in the store until it expires via `SessionTimeout` or is explicitly deleted
- **Blazor Server reconnect** (WebSocket drop within timeout) — the *same* circuit is reconnected, the *same* scoped service instances are reused, so `CircuitSessionId` stays the same → the UI seamlessly picks up where it left off via `TryResumeActiveRunAsync`
- **Multi-tab** → each tab has its own circuit, GUID, and conversation history — they are completely independent

#### Pattern 2 — Explicit from the frontend (consumer-provided)

The consumer page sets `SessionId` explicitly:

```razor
@* Page explicitly supplies a stable ID *@
<AgentChatSurface SessionId="support-ticket-1042" />

@* Or driven by the layout's computed value *@
@* DemoLayout.razor pattern: *@
private string AssistantSessionId =>
    $"demo:{_assistantClientId}:{CurrentRoutePath.TrimEnd('/').ToLowerInvariant()}";
```

The consumer (frontend Blazor component) is the **owner** — it decides the value and passes it down. The runtime never overrides an explicit `SessionId`.

#### Pattern 3 — From the remote chat client (WASM / external HTTP)

For the remote (HTTP-based) chat scenario, the client sends `SessionId` in the POST body:

```typescript
// Client-side (not necessarily Blazor)
POST /agentblazor/chat/run
{
    "userMessage": "Hello",
    "sessionId": "my-external-session-id",  // ← client decides
    "userId": "user-abc-123"
}
```

The `AgentRemoteChatSurface` component defaults to a new GUID per instance if the consumer doesn't set one:

```razor
@* AgentRemoteChatSurface.razor *@
[Parameter] public string SessionId { get; set; } = $"remote-chat-{Guid.NewGuid():N}";
```

#### Pattern 4 — From the route or user identity

The hosting page derives `SessionId` from application context:

```razor
@* From route parameter *@
@page "/chat/{SessionSlug?}"
<AgentChatSurface SessionId="@SessionSlug" />

@* From authenticated user *@
@inject AuthenticationStateProvider Auth
<AgentChatSurface SessionId="@_mySessionId" />
@code {
    private string _mySessionId = "global";
    protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
    {
        var auth = await Auth.GetAuthenticationStateAsync();
        var user = auth.User;
        if (user.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true)
            _mySessionId = $"user:{user.FindFirst(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier)!.Value}";
    }
}
```

#### Fallback chain (both component and API layers)

```
Component layer:         SessionId param → CircuitSessionId (GUID) [→ "global"]
API layer (remote):      SessionId field → Context["session_id"] [→ "global"]
Storage layer:           BuildSessionKey(sessionId, agent, isolation)
                         └─ isolation ON:  "{id}::agent::{name}"
                         └─ isolation OFF: "{id}" (raw sessionId)
```

### How SessionId Is Persisted in Each Store

#### InMemoryConversationStore

```csharp
// Key type: string with OrdinalIgnoreCase comparer
private readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, ConversationHistory> _sessions =
    new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);

// On AppendTurnAsync: the sessionId parameter IS the dictionary key
_sessions.AddOrUpdate(
    sessionId,                              // ← the key
    _ => ConversationHistory.Create(sessionId).WithTurn(turn),
    (_, existing) => existing.WithTurn(turn));

// On GetHistoryAsync: lookup by the same key
_sessions.TryGetValue(sessionId, out var history);
```

The `ConversationHistory` record stored as the value also carries a `SessionId` field, but the **dictionary key** is the authoritative storage identifier. The `SessionId` property on the record is informational (used when serializing to JSON for the file store).

**User index**: A secondary `ConcurrentDictionary<string, HashSet<string>>` maps userId → set of sessionIds.

#### JsonFileConversationStore

```csharp
// Same in-memory dictionary as InMemory, PLUS file persistence
private sealed record ConversationStoreSnapshot(
    IReadOnlyDictionary<string, ConversationHistory> Sessions);

// Serialized to disk as:
// {
//   "sessions": {
//     "demo:client123:/workflows/support": { "sessionId": "...", "turns": [...] },
//     "my-session": { "sessionId": "...", "turns": [...] }
//   }
// }

private async Task PersistSnapshotAsync(CancellationToken ct)
{
    var snapshot = new ConversationStoreSnapshot(
        _sessions.ToDictionary(kvp => kvp.Key, kvp => kvp.Value, StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase));

    // Atomic write via temp file + rename
    var tempPath = _filePath + ".tmp";
    await using (var stream = File.Create(tempPath))
        await JsonSerializer.SerializeAsync(stream, snapshot, SerializerOptions, ct);
    File.Move(tempPath, _filePath, overwrite: true);
}
```

The JSON file is a **flat dictionary** — sessionId strings are JSON object keys. No relational schema, no indexes. The serializer writes the `ConversationHistory` record (including its `SessionId` field) as the value.

On startup, `LoadSnapshot()` deserializes the JSON back into the `ConcurrentDictionary`:

```csharp
private void LoadSnapshot()
{
    using var stream = File.OpenRead(_filePath);
    var snapshot = JsonSerializer.Deserialize<ConversationStoreSnapshot>(stream, SerializerOptions);
    foreach (var pair in snapshot.Sessions)
    {
        _sessions[pair.Key] = pair.Value;   // ← pair.Key is the sessionId
        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(pair.Value.UserId))
            AddToUserIndex(pair.Key, pair.Value.UserId);
    }
}
```

#### EF Core Custom Store (pattern)

A custom `IConversationStore` using EF Core would store SessionId as a primary key:

```csharp
public class ConversationHistoryEntity
{
    // SessionId IS the primary key — string, case-insensitive collation
    [Key]
    [MaxLength(512)]
    public string SessionId { get; set; }

    public string TurnsJson { get; set; }          // JSON-serialized turns
    public DateTime CreatedAt { get; set; }
    public DateTime LastActivityAt { get; set; }
    public string? UserId { get; set; }
}

// In OnModelCreating:
entity.Property(e => e.SessionId)
      .UseCollation("SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS");  // case-insensitive
```

The full EF Core store implementation is documented in the [ab-conversation-store](../ab-conversation-store/SKILL.md) skill.

## Entity-Level Session Identity

For the entity schema implications (canonical `ConversationSessionEntity` columns, indexes, `BuildSessionKey()` → column mapping), see [ab-entity-design/references/session-identity-entities.md](../ab-entity-design/references/session-identity-entities.md).

### How `IsolateConversationsByAgent` affects entity rows

**Dual-trigger condition** (`AgentChatSurface.razor` line ~647):

```
ShouldIsolateConversationSession =
    AgentBlazorOptionsAccessor.Value.IsolateConversationsByAgent  (default: true)
    && _agentNames.Count > 1                                       (chat surface has >1 agent)
```

Both conditions must be true — single-agent chat surfaces never isolate, regardless of the option setting.

#### ISOLATION ON — concrete user interaction

Imagine a support dashboard with two registered agents: "SupportAgent" and "InboxAgent".

1. **User opens the page** → browser tab = one Blazor Server SignalR circuit → GUID `"d1e9a3f2"`
2. **AgentChatSurface renders** with a `<select>` dropdown:

   ```
   ┌─────────────────────────┐
   │ Agent: [SupportAgent ▾] │  ← user can pick any agent
   └─────────────────────────┘
   ```

3. **User selects "SupportAgent"**, types "Show open tickets", hits Enter
   - Store key = `"d1e9a3f2::agent::SupportAgent"`
   - `ConversationSessionEntity` row created with `SessionId = "d1e9a3f2::agent::SupportAgent"`
   - 3 turns accumulate: user asks, agent replies, user follows up, agent replies

4. **User switches dropdown to "InboxAgent"**
   - `HydrateTimelineFromHistoryAsync()` fires on parameter change
   - `GetHistoryAsync("d1e9a3f2::agent::InboxAgent")` → returns `null` (fresh agent, no history yet)
   - **Chat timeline CLEARS** — the SupportAgent conversation disappears from view
   - User types "Check unread messages", hits Enter
   - Store key = `"d1e9a3f2::agent::InboxAgent"`
   - **NEW** `ConversationSessionEntity` row created — second row sharing `BaseSessionId = "d1e9a3f2"`

5. **User switches BACK to "SupportAgent"** in the dropdown
   - `GetHistoryAsync("d1e9a3f2::agent::SupportAgent")` → returns the 3-turn history from step 3
   - **Timeline repopulates** with the previous SupportAgent conversation — it was preserved!

**Entity state after this session:**

```
ConversationSessionEntity { Id=1, SessionId="d1e9a3f2::agent::SupportAgent",
    BaseSessionId="d1e9a3f2", AgentName="SupportAgent" }
  └── ConversationTurnEntity × 3

ConversationSessionEntity { Id=2, SessionId="d1e9a3f2::agent::InboxAgent",
    BaseSessionId="d1e9a3f2", AgentName="InboxAgent" }
  └── ConversationTurnEntity × 1
```

**Session browser behavior:** `GetActiveSessionsAsync()` returns **TWO** entries — the user sees both sessions listed separately.

#### ISOLATION OFF — concrete user interaction

Same setup but `IsolateConversationsByAgent = false` (or only 1 agent registered).

1. User opens the page → circuit GUID `"d1e9a3f2"`
2. AgentChatSurface renders with dropdown, user picks "SupportAgent"
3. User types "Show open tickets", hits Enter
   - Store key = `"d1e9a3f2"` (no agent suffix — `BuildSessionKey` ignores `agentName` when isolation OFF)
   - `ConversationSessionEntity` row created with `SessionId = "d1e9a3f2"`

4. **User switches dropdown to "InboxAgent"**
   - `GetHistoryAsync("d1e9a3f2")` → returns the **SAME** history from step 3
   - **Timeline does NOT clear** — the SupportAgent conversation is still visible!
   - User types "Check unread messages"
   - Store key = still `"d1e9a3f2"` — appended to the **SAME** session
   - Now the LLM sees: "Show open tickets" + agent reply + "Check unread messages" + agent reply
     **BUT both turns were addressed to/from DIFFERENT agents** — context is interleaved

**Entity state after this session:**

```
ConversationSessionEntity { Id=1, SessionId="d1e9a3f2",
    BaseSessionId="d1e9a3f2", AgentName=null }
  └── ConversationTurnEntity × 4 (mixed SupportAgent + InboxAgent turns)
```

**Risk:** The LLM receives a history where turns alternate between different agent personas. It may not understand that "Check unread messages" was directed at InboxAgent, not SupportAgent.

#### Agent handoff path (`/agent` command)

- User types `/agent InboxAgent` in the chat input → `CompleteHandoffAsync()` sets `_selectedAgent = "InboxAgent"`
- Same hydration logic applies — isolation determines whether history is scoped or shared
- `AgentChatBar` (single-agent widget variant) also uses `BuildSessionKey` with its `AgentName` parameter

### Query patterns for EF Core stores

| Query | Isolation ON (multi-agent) | Isolation OFF (or single agent) |
|---|---|---|
| "All sessions for this circuit" | `WHERE BaseSessionId = "abc123"` → returns N rows (one per agent) | `WHERE SessionId = "abc123"` → returns 1 row |
| "History for current agent" | `WHERE SessionId = "abc123::agent::SupportAgent"` | `WHERE SessionId = "abc123"` (agent name irrelevant) |
| "All sessions for tenant + user" | `WHERE TenantId = @t AND UserId = @u` | Same (TenantId + UserId unaffected by isolation) |

#### Summary: SessionId Across Stores

| Store | Key location | Key type | Equality | Lookup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `InMemoryConversationStore` | `ConcurrentDictionary` key | `string` | `OrdinalIgnoreCase` | O(1) hash lookup |
| `JsonFileConversationStore` | JSON object key | `string` | `OrdinalIgnoreCase` (at runtime); JSON key (on file read) | O(1) dict + file round-trip per mutation |
| EF Core (custom) | Primary key column | `nvarchar(512)` | DB collation | PK index seek |

## Backend: Session Key Isolation

`AgentConversationScope.BuildSessionKey()` scopes conversation history when multiple agents share one circuit:

```csharp
// isolation OFF: "my-session"
// isolation ON:  "my-session::agent::SupportAgent"

// Controlled by:
options.IsolateConversationsByAgent  // AgentBlazorOptions
```

The chat surface's `ShouldIsolateConversationSession` is `true` only when `IsolateConversationsByAgent` is enabled AND `_agentNames.Count > 1`.

**Important**: The session key used for storage is the isolated key (`EffectiveConversationSessionId`), not the raw `SessionId`. When calling `GetHistoryAsync()` from a UI component, use the same isolated key.

> [!WARNING]
> **Wrong** — returns `null` when isolation is enabled:
> ```csharp
> var history = await store.GetHistoryAsync("my-session");
> ```
> **Right** — use `BuildSessionKey` to compute the storage key:
> ```csharp
> var key = AgentConversationScope.BuildSessionKey("my-session", agentName, isolateByAgent: true);
> var history = await store.GetHistoryAsync(key);
> ```

## Backend: Session Events

`IAgentChatSessionEvents` (singleton) fires after each turn is persisted:

```csharp
public interface IAgentChatSessionEvents
{
    event Action<AgentChatSessionUpdate>? SessionUpdated;
    void NotifySessionUpdated(string sessionId, string sourceId);
}

// AgentChatSessionUpdate contains:
//   SessionId — the EffectiveConversationSessionId
//   SourceId  — the component instance ID
```

Use this to synchronize multiple chat surfaces on the same page (e.g., update a session list when a new turn completes).

> **Render-mode note**: `IConversationStore` is a singleton. In Blazor Server, all circuits share one store. In WebAssembly, each client process has its own store instance (or connects via the remote chat API). During prerendering, `GetHistoryAsync` returns `null` because no turns have been stored yet — the first `AppendTurnAsync` creates the session entry.
